content_data.heading: Practical AI systems built to work in your business
content_data.body_text: We build AI systems for businesses that have real work to get done. That means automation pipelines, private model deployments, data collection at scale, and agent systems that handle complex tasks without constant supervision. We don't push a single platform or vendor. We pick whatever works best for the job, and we're straightforward when AI isn't the right answer.

content_data.headline: How we actually deploy AI inside a business
content_data.subheadline: Picking the right model is the easy part. The work is making it survive contact with your real data, your real staff, and your real edge cases. If you want a quick read on where your business stands before that work starts, try our AI Project Readiness Checker.

content_data.content:
We pick the model that suits the task, not the vendor we happen to prefer. A document summary, a piece of code, and a reasoning-heavy decision often need three different tools underneath. Tying a business to a single provider means inheriting that provider's weak spots along with its strengths, so we don't do it.

Your data stays yours. That can mean a privately hosted model, a version fine-tuned on your own records using techniques like LoRA, or a model that runs entirely in the browser and never leaves the machine it's on. For a firm handling client files or financial records, that's not a compliance checkbox, it's the actual reason AI adoption stalls in the first place.

Every system we build has review gates you configure yourself. You decide what gets automated outright and what needs a human to sign off before it moves. Nothing runs as a black box that produces answers you can't trace back to a source.

Systems also keep improving after they go live. Automated quality sweeps catch drift and errors between review cycles, and where a system does research or writes content, it checks facts against named sources before publishing anything. That doesn't mean the output is always right, only that you can see where it came from and check it yourself. You can read more about how a project actually runs on how we work, or see the range of systems this covers on our services page. If you're not sure whether now is the right moment to start, our AI Project Readiness Checker is a short way to find out. It's a set of questions about your data, your team, and your budget clarity, and it flags what needs sorting before any consultancy, including us, gets involved. If you want the fuller argument for why we build this way, it's laid out in our position on AI.

content_data.headline: What every deployment we build has in common
content_data.subheadline: These aren't marketing lines. They're the working rules we apply whether we're building a quoting pipeline for a logistics firm or an agent network running research at scale.

questions.answer: We start with the task, not a favourite vendor. Some jobs suit a large reasoning model, others run better on a smaller, cheaper model fine-tuned on your own documents. We've built with Llama, Mistral, Phi, and several proprietary models, and we mix them where it makes sense, one model drafting text, another checking facts, another handling structured data. The result is a system built for the job in front of us, not whatever a single provider happens to sell.
questions.question: How do you decide which AI model to use for our business?

questions.answer: Not unless you want it to. We deploy private hosting, local models, and in-browser models specifically so client data never has to touch a third-party server. Where we do use hosted models, we set them up so your data isn't retained or used for training. This matters more to finance and compliance leads than most vendors admit, so we treat it as a design decision from day one, not a policy document bolted on afterwards.
questions.question: Does our data leave our building or get used to train someone else's model?

questions.answer: It will, occasionally, get something wrong. That's why we build human review gates into the parts of a system where a mistake actually costs you money or trust, and automate freely everywhere else. You decide what needs a person's eyes before it goes out and what doesn't. Nothing runs as a black box that you're expected to trust blindly.
questions.question: What happens if the AI gets something wrong?

questions.answer: No. We build primarily on open-weight models like Llama, Mistral, and Phi, fine-tuned for your specific use with methods like LoRA and DoRA. If a provider changes their pricing or their terms, you're not stuck. Vendor lock-in is a real cost that's easy to ignore until the bill changes, so we design around it from the start.
questions.question: Are we locked into one AI provider once you've built our system?

questions.answer: No, but you do need someone internally who owns the process the system supports. We handle the model selection, training, and infrastructure. Your team's job is knowing which quotes look wrong, which documents need a second read, and telling us when the business itself changes. That division of labour is described in more detail on our how we work page.
questions.question: Do we need our own technical team to run this once it's live?

questions.answer: It depends on the task and how much your data needs cleaning before a model can use it. A quoting or document-screening system tends to move faster than a multi-agent pipeline handling thousands of records. We'd rather give you a scope on a call than a number that sounds good in a brief. Before that call, try our AI Project Readiness Checker. It's a short set of questions on your data, team, and infrastructure that gives you a read on what's likely to slow things down, and it can be wrong in either direction, so treat it as a starting point rather than a verdict. Book a discovery call and we'll tell you what's realistic for your case specifically.
questions.question: How long does it take to get a working system in place?

questions.answer: No. We run automated quality sweeps after launch so the system keeps getting better between the times a human actually looks at it. That's different to most AI projects, which get tuned once at launch and then quietly drift. If you want to see what that looks like in practice, our case studies describe a few of these systems running in production.
questions.question: Does the system just stop improving once it's launched?

questions.answer: No, and we'll say so. If a process is broken, badly documented, or changes every month depending on who's covering for whom, automating it just breaks it faster and with more confidence. Sometimes the recommendation is to fix the process first and revisit AI afterwards. We've written about this directly on our position on AI page, and we'd rather lose a sale than sell you a system that fails in month two.

content_data.headline: What we've built and who it helped
content_data.subheadline: Each project below started as a specific operational problem. Here's the approach we took and what changed as a result.

case_studies.title: AI-Powered Website Generation for SMEs
case_studies.results: Multiple production sites running autonomously. Each site receives industry-specific content, relevant interactive tools, and ongoing quality improvements without manual intervention. SME owners get a professional web presence without the typical agency timeline or cost.
case_studies.summary: Built an AI system that takes a domain name and autonomously creates a complete business website — researching the industry, writing targeted content, designing appropriate visuals, generating interactive tools, and deploying to production. The system understands different industries and adapts its output accordingly, from gas wholesalers to consulting firms.

case_studies.title: Automated Data Collection and Business Verification
case_studies.results: Thousands of verified practice records with financial enrichment data. What would take a research team weeks runs continuously and autonomously, with built-in quality checks at every stage.
case_studies.summary: Deployed AI agents to collect, verify, and enrich veterinary practice data across the UK. The system discovers practices by area, extracts structured information, then cross-references against Companies House to verify legitimacy — catching dissolved businesses and incomplete registrations automatically.

case_studies.title: Intelligent Tool Suggestion and Generation
case_studies.results: Industry-specific tools deployed across multiple sites with companion guides and automatic cross-referencing from related content pages. The system handles everything from tool concept through to live deployment.
case_studies.summary: The AI evaluates what interactive tools would genuinely help a website's visitors based on their industry and needs — then builds and deploys those tools automatically. A gas wholesaler gets fuel cost calculators and unit converters; a consulting firm gets ROI estimators. No irrelevant suggestions, no manual development.

case_studies.title: Automated News Collection with Credibility Filtering
case_studies.results: Automated news sections running on production sites with six-hour refresh cycles. Source credibility tracking means businesses only display verified, relevant industry news — building authority without editorial overhead.
case_studies.summary: Built a multi-source news pipeline that collects from RSS, web search, and AI-powered search simultaneously. An AI triage layer scores every item for relevance to the business and credibility of the source — distinguishing Reuters from anonymous social media posts before anything reaches the live site.

content_data.heading: Book a Discovery Call
content_data.form_description: Tell us a little about what you're trying to solve. We'll read it before the call, so you won't spend the first ten minutes explaining your business from scratch. No obligation — if AI isn't the right fit, we'll say so.

content_data.intro_text: No sales pitch. No obligation. If you have a process that feels like it should not require this much manual effort, tell us about it. We will give you a view of whether AI can help, what it would involve, and what it would cost. If it is not the right fit, we will say so.

questions.answer: No. You need only to know your own business. We handle the technical side and explain everything in plain language. Our job is to understand your problem first — the technology comes second. If we recommend something, we will tell you why in terms that make sense to you, not in terms that require a computer science degree. You will never be expected to know what a model is, how fine-tuning works, or what a vector database does. That is our concern, not yours.
questions.question: Do I need to understand AI to work with you?

questions.answer: We spend around 30 to 45 minutes asking about your business — what you do, where the friction is, and what you have already tried. We are not running a sales script. We are trying to work out whether there is a genuine problem we can help with. At the end, we will give you a view of whether AI is likely to help, roughly what an approach might look like, and what it would cost to find out more. No pressure, no follow-up sequence, no proposal sent before you ask for one.
questions.question: What actually happens on a discovery call?

questions.answer: It depends on what you need, and we will not pretend otherwise. A focused automation for a single workflow costs far less than a multi-agent system processing thousands of documents. What we can tell you is that we work with SMEs, not enterprise budgets, and we scope projects to match what makes financial sense for the size of the problem. On the discovery call we will give you a realistic range once we understand what we are dealing with. If the numbers do not stack up, we will say so.
questions.question: What does it cost?

questions.answer: Smaller projects — a focused automation, a RAG system over your internal documents, a data pipeline — typically take two to six weeks from kick-off to working system. More complex builds involving multiple agent systems or custom model training take longer. We will give you a realistic timeline before any work begins, and we do not start the clock until the scope is agreed. We would rather set a timeline and hit it than promise speed we cannot deliver.
questions.question: How long does a typical project take?

questions.answer: Then we will tell you that on the call. There are plenty of situations where AI adds cost and complexity without adding value — and we have no interest in building something that does not work. Our reputation depends on projects that actually solve problems, not on closing every conversation. If a simpler tool, a process change, or just better software would serve you better, we will say so. We would rather lose a project than deliver something that disappoints.
questions.question: What if AI is not the right answer for my business?

questions.answer: Your data stays yours. We do not use your business data to train models on your behalf without explicit agreement, and we never pass it to third-party AI providers without your knowledge. For organisations with stricter requirements, we can deploy models that run entirely within your own infrastructure — nothing leaves your environment. We treat data privacy as a genuine business concern, not a checkbox. If you have GDPR or regulatory obligations, we factor those in from the start, not as an afterthought.
questions.question: What happens to our data? Is it safe?

questions.answer: Yes, and that is most of our clients. You do not need existing AI tools, a technical team, or any prior experience with automation. We assess what you have, work with it where possible, and build only what is needed. We have helped businesses go from no AI capability at all to running systems that handle meaningful volumes of work — without requiring them to hire a data scientist or change how their team operates day to day.

content_data.headline: The systems we build, and the problems they solve

content_data.content:
Most of the services listed above sound like variations on a theme: pipelines, models, data. The differences matter more than they look, because the wrong choice for your problem will waste months even if the technology works perfectly. So before we build anything, we work out which of these actually fits what you are trying to solve, and we say so plainly if none of them do.

That starts with the problem, not the technology. A repetitive admin task usually calls for an automation pipeline: a sequence of steps that used to need a person and now does not, though a review gate can sit at any point where you want a human to check the work before it goes further. A question your staff keep asking about internal policy or past client work usually calls for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), where the AI searches your own documents for an answer instead of guessing from what it learned on the internet. A task where the AI needs to sound like your industry rather than a generic assistant usually calls for fine-tuning, training a model on your own material using efficient methods such as LoRA or DoRA so the adjustment is quick and affordable rather than a full retrain.

We are not attached to one AI provider, and we do not pretend one model is right for every job. Open-weight models such as Llama, Mistral, or Phi get used where running things privately on your own infrastructure matters, commercial models get used where they are simply better at the task, and the decision is made on that basis rather than on which vendor we happen to prefer. Where your data is involved, whether that is emails, financial records, or client files, it stays under your control unless you decide otherwise. If you want a sense of where your own data handling stands before you talk to us, our GDPR and AI data risk self-assessment walks through the questions a compliance lead would ask, though it can only point you in a direction, not replace proper advice on your specific setup.

If you are not sure which of this applies to you, that is a perfectly normal place to start. See how we work through a project from first call to a running system, or get in touch and describe the problem in your own words. We will tell you plainly if AI is not the right answer.

content_data.headline: What We Help Businesses Do

use_cases.title: Automating Client Intake and Request Screening
use_cases.results: Teams get back hours each week previously spent on manual triage. Response times improve. No genuine enquiry gets missed because someone was busy.
use_cases.summary: Many service businesses spend hours each week reading incoming enquiries, deciding which are worth pursuing, and routing them to the right person. We build AI systems that read, categorise, and triage incoming requests automatically — flagging high-priority leads, filtering out time-wasters, and drafting initial responses for review. Staff approve what goes out. The system handles the volume.

use_cases.title: Searching and Summarising Internal Documents
use_cases.results: Staff stop digging through folders and start getting answers in seconds. Onboarding new team members becomes faster. Institutional knowledge stops walking out the door.
use_cases.summary: When your knowledge lives across emails, shared drives, PDFs, and old reports, finding the right information takes too long. We deploy RAG systems that let your team ask plain-English questions and get accurate answers drawn from your own documents — contracts, policies, past proposals, financial records, whatever you have. The AI cites its sources so staff can verify what they're reading.

use_cases.title: Generating Quotes and Proposals at Scale
use_cases.results: Quote turnaround drops from days to minutes. Estimators spend their time on complex jobs rather than routine paperwork. Win rates improve when responses go out faster.
use_cases.summary: Putting together quotes is repetitive work that pulls skilled people away from the jobs that actually make money. We build automated quoting pipelines that take structured inputs — job type, size, materials, location — and produce accurate, formatted proposals ready for review and sending. Staff check the output and approve it. The system does the drafting.

use_cases.title: Monitoring Competitor and Market Data
use_cases.results: Businesses stay informed without the manual effort. Pricing decisions and marketing responses happen faster because the data is already there.
use_cases.summary: Keeping track of what competitors are doing — pricing changes, new product lines, promotional activity — is time-consuming to do manually and easy to let slip. We build data collection pipelines that monitor thousands of web sources automatically, structure the information, and surface what's relevant. You get a clear picture of the market without anyone having to spend hours on research.

use_cases.title: Extracting Data from Financial and Company Records
use_cases.client: Finance, Compliance and Due Diligence Teams
use_cases.results: Due diligence that used to take days can be completed in a fraction of the time. Teams get consistent, structured data rather than inconsistent manual extracts.
use_cases.summary: Pulling structured information from Companies House filings, regulatory documents, and public financial records is slow, error-prone work when done by hand. We build pipelines that collect, parse, and organise this data automatically — at scale, across thousands of companies if needed. The result is clean, structured data ready for analysis rather than a stack of PDFs to wade through.

use_cases.title: Running AI on Sensitive Data Without Sending It Externally
use_cases.client: Healthcare Admin, Legal and Financial Services
use_cases.results: Businesses in regulated sectors can use AI without compromising on data security. Staff get powerful tools. Clients and regulators stay reassured.
use_cases.summary: Some businesses can't send client data to third-party AI providers — whether for regulatory reasons, client confidentiality, or simple data governance. We deploy private AI systems that run locally or within your own infrastructure. No data leaves your environment. You get the productivity benefits of AI without the compliance risk.

use_cases.title: Building and Deploying Agent Systems for Complex Workflows
use_cases.results: Complex multi-step processes that previously required significant human coordination can run largely automatically, with people stepping in to approve rather than to execute.
use_cases.summary: Some tasks are too complex for a single AI model — they require research, decision-making, verification, and action across multiple steps. We design and deploy networks of AI agents that work together to handle these workflows: gathering information, checking facts, making decisions, and passing results between each other. Human review gates are built in wherever approval matters.

use_cases.title: Training AI Models on Your Own Business Data
use_cases.client: Businesses with Specialist Knowledge or Terminology
use_cases.results: AI outputs that fit your business from day one rather than needing constant correction. Models that understand your terminology, tone, and context without having to be told every time.
use_cases.summary: General AI models don't know your industry's language, your product catalogue, your pricing logic, or your way of doing things. We fine-tune models on your specific data using efficient training techniques — so the AI you use actually understands your business. This isn't prompt engineering. It's a model that has genuinely learned from your content.
